history.administration_response: The Administration stated that it would continue to review the current policies and methodology in place with a view towards creating a more appropriate methodology that better suited the general peacekeeping operations risk environment. In addition, the Business Transformation and Accountability Division would continue to work with all the other components of the accountability system to streamline the enterprise risk management process and develop risk-based approaches to strengthen the resilience, effectiveness and efficiency of peacekeeping operations. Further strengthening of the coordination efforts between the Office of Programme Planning, Finance and Budget and the Business Transformation and Accountability Division in the ongoing deployment of the Umoja enterprise risk management module within the internal control framework would also contribute towards the simplification of the overall accountability requirements for peacekeeping operations. The integration of the internal control framework with enterprise risk management processes would continue through the standardization of the internal controls included in the risk registers for peacekeeping operations.
history.board_assessment: Work is still ongoing. The Board considers the recommendation to be under implementation.

history.administration_response: The Administration stated that considerable progress had been made during the reporting period. A detailed inventory of reporting requirements was developed and used to identify opportunities to simplify reporting requests from Headquarters departments. Proposals under review or implementation range from filling data gaps from existing sources, automating reporting when data exist in Umoja and creating interface/data transfers between reporting platforms across departments. Obsolete paper-based forms have been decommissioned and a peer review process was established to inform the design of new reporting requirements, allowing for the sharing of ideas on existing data sources and lessons learned. The next phase of the project will continue to explore the feasibility of opportunities to rationalize and tailor or stop reporting requirements.
history.board_assessment: The Board notes the progress made and will be attentive to further positive developments.

history.sg_progress: Considerable progress has been made towards streamlining and reducing the burden on managers. A detailed inventory of reporting requirements was developed and used to identify significant opportunities to simplify reporting requests from Headquarters. The proposals under review or implementation range from filling data gaps, automating reporting when data exist in Umoja and creating interface and data transfers between reporting platforms across departments. Obsolete paper-based forms have been decommissioned, and a peer review process has been established to inform the design of new reporting requirements, allowing for the sharing of ideas on existing data sources and lessons learned. The next phase of the project will continue to explore the feasibility of opportunities to rationalize and tailor or stop reporting requirements. Envisaged benefits include but are not limited to: (a) Reducing the overall number, complexity or frequency of reporting requirements; (b) Increasing automation and data-sharing; (c) Removing reporting duplications or closing data gaps to better support decision-making; (d) Adopting new approaches to reporting processes, such as by tailoring requirements or sampling entities, on the basis of relevance and mandates. An implementation schedule is being developed to outline the planned review sequence.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration conduct a thorough review of all the existing accountability requirements on peacekeeping operations, in order to streamline and reduce the burden on managers (“simplification shock”), as well as to better articulate risk management with key internal control, strategic programming, budgeting and performance frameworks and ensure data- sharing and interconnected information systems.
history.administration_response: The Administration requests the closure of this recommendation because it was implemented. The Administration conducted a thorough review of all existing accountability and reporting requirements across the United Nations Secretariat. The review was completed in March 2025, and the results were shared with all entities. The results framework comprises approximately 185 reports, ranging in frequency from daily to annual and ad hoc, across all thematic areas. On the basis of an analysis of this inventory, 26 areas were identified in order to streamline reporting processes and reduce the administrative burden on managers. The focus of the review was on eliminating duplication, automating data collection, simplifying and tailoring content, reducing reporting frequency and adjusting reporting timelines to align more closely with business cycles. The Administration will prioritize these proposals for detailed feasibility reviews and subsequent implementation in the context of the UN80 Initiative. A copy of the review (with an inventory of reporting requirements) was provided to the Board as evidence of implementation.
history.board_assessment: The Board recognizes the efforts made and the forthcoming structural changes made in the light of the context, in particular the UN80 Initiative. Given the progress already made, the Board considers the recommendation to be implemented.
